description: Expand seed data to include a second domain (Computer Science), a second module, 7 user accounts (4 learners, 2 instructors, 1 admin), and update the demo user switcher to allow switching between individual users (not just roles). Also update the AppProvider to support per-user context and the navigation to show a user picker in demo mode.
steps: 1. In src/lib/domain/types.ts, add a DemoUserWithDomain type or extend DemoUser to include a domainId field so we know which domain each user is associated with. Keep existing DemoUser type unchanged for backward compatibility - add optional domainId.

2. In src/lib/data/seed.ts, add a second domain: { id: 'domain-2', name: 'Computer Science', description: 'Programming fundamentals, algorithms, data structures, and software development practices', complianceLabel: 'Academic Integrity' }. Export it alongside the existing domain (rename 'domain' export to 'domains' array or export both individually).

3. In src/lib/data/seed.ts, add a second module for Computer Science: { id: 'module-2', domainId: 'domain-2', title: 'Introduction to Sorting Algorithms', description: 'Understand fundamental sorting algorithms, their time complexities, trade-offs, and appropriate use cases before implementing them in practical exercises.', ownerId: 'user-instructor-2', status: 'published', activeVersionId: 'version-2', estimatedMinutes: 20 }. Add corresponding moduleVersion, objectives, competencies (e.g., Algorithm Analysis, Implementation Patterns, Edge Cases, Optimization), activities (5-7 guided steps covering bubble/selection/merge/quick sort with complexity analysis), and 5 assessment questions (2 critical relating to algorithm correctness). Follow the exact same patterns as the existing module-1 data.

4. In src/lib/data/seed.ts, expand demoUsers to 7 accounts: learner Alex Tan (user-learner-1, domain-1), learner Rachel Ng (user-learner-2, domain-1), learner Jordan Lee (user-learner-3, domain-2), learner Mei Chen (user-learner-4, domain-2), instructor Dr Sarah Lim (user-instructor-1, domain-1), instructor Prof David Tan (user-instructor-2, domain-2), admin Daniel Wong (user-admin-1). Each user gets domainId to indicate their primary domain assignment.

5. Update moduleRegistry in seed.ts to include the new Computer Science module with Prof David Tan as owner. Update the existing 'module-2' entry (Oscilloscope) to become 'module-3' or rename it, and make the CS module 'module-2'.
6. Add cohort metrics, misconceptions, and intervention data for the CS module (following the same structure as existing electrical module data) so the CS instructor has data to view.

7. In src/components/navigation.tsx, replace the simple role switcher with a user picker dropdown in demo mode. Show all 7 users grouped by role. When a user is selected, update both the current user AND the role. The existing role switcher buttons can remain as quick shortcuts but selecting a user should take precedence.

8. In src/components/providers.tsx, update AppProvider: (a) add state for selectedDemoUserId (defaults to 'user-learner-1'), (b) derive currentUser from selectedDemoUserId rather than just finding first user with matching role, (c) add setCurrentDemoUser(userId) function to context, (d) when a demo user is selected, also update the role accordingly. The role setter should also switch to the first user of that role (for backward compat with the role shortcut buttons).
9. Update src/lib/persistence.ts PersistedState interface to include selectedDemoUserId so demo user selection persists across refreshes.
10. Ensure all existing imports of seed data (domain, learningModule, demoUsers, cohortMetrics, etc.) continue to work. If exports are renamed, update all import sites. Run typecheck to confirm.
acceptance_criteria: demoUsers array contains exactly 7 users with correct roles and domain assignments
A second domain 'Computer Science' exists in seed data with its own module, competencies, activities, and questions
The navigation user picker shows all 7 demo users grouped by role
Switching demo users updates both currentUser and role in context
Selected demo user persists across page refresh via localStorage
All existing tests pass (pnpm run test -- --run)

findings: All 56 existing tests pass. Build and typecheck succeed. The existing 'domain' and 'learningModule' exports remain unchanged for backward compatibility. New CS data is exported as separate named exports (csModule, csModuleVersion, csCompetencies, etc.). The moduleRegistry now has 3 entries with the CS module as module-2 and the Oscilloscope draft as module-3. The navigation now has both role shortcut buttons AND a user picker dropdown. setCurrentDemoUser is available in the app context.
